what: caption.py --srt with --offset, --max-lines or the ASS route lost the text of a cue that was only full-width digits (１２３) before a timing line with no blank line above it, and the result said completed, verified: true, cues: 2; a timing line written in those digits passed parse_srt() and the shared-grammar check, so a dry run completed and the real run failed in ffmpeg (Invalid data found when processing input) or burned the line as text; validate_color() passed red@0. with a full-width 5 and color.py --lut counted a .cube's size and rows in those digits, both refused by ffmpeg after a completed dry run
escaped: Python's str.isdigit(), float() and an re pattern's \d take every Unicode digit, ffmpeg's SRT reader, av_parse_color() and lut3d take 0-9, and every SRT, colour and LUT fixture was written in ASCII; #414's shared-grammar check compared the two readers' grammars with \d on our side, so it measured agreement with a pattern wider than the reader it described
mechanism: srt_blocks() takes an index as [0-9]+ and _SRT_CUE_START, _SHARED_SRT_TIMING and _COLOR_TOKEN_RE are re.ASCII; srt_file_blocks(), now the one reader of a caller's SRT for parse_srt() and srt_timings_shared_grammar(), refuses a timing line in other digits as kind input with the hint to write them in ASCII, and refuse_bad_cube() reads the size and rows in ASCII only. test_a_cue_of_full_width_digits_is_text_as_ffmpeg_reads_it compares parse_srt() with ffmpeg's own reading of the file; test_a_timing_line_in_other_digits_is_refused_before_ffmpeg_runs covers the first, a later and an unseparated timing line in dry and real runs, the colour and both .cube cases; the claim class's guard (test_guards.SweepGuards) stands
